paper_a.title: A motivated exposition of the proof of Tverberg's theorem

metadata.description: Paper A (Retinskiy-Ryabichev-Skopenkov) is an expository proof of the classical Tverberg theorem (case r=3) via lifting and the Colorful Caratheodory theorem. Paper B (Fulek-Gartner-Kupavskii-Valtr-Wagner) takes Tverberg as a cited starting point and strengthens it to the Crossing Tverberg theorem, in which the convex hulls of the parts not only share a point but pairwise cross. The relationship is EXT: paper B extends the base theorem proved in paper A to a richer geometric conclusion (crossing hulls), with substantial new combinatorial machinery (cocycles, parity lemma, unnesting lemma, fixing-pairs algorithm) that has no counterpart in paper A.

matches.explanation: Both nodes state the classical Tverberg theorem in identical form: any (d+1)(r-1)+1 points in R^d admit a partition into r parts whose convex hulls share a common point. In paper A this is the main result being proved expositorily; in paper B it is cited as Tverberg 1966 (origin: external) and used as the starting point for the crossing strengthening. The cross-origin (paper-contribution vs cited-prior-work) match is exactly the signal §'Origin-aware filtering' flags as evidence for EXT.

Paper A's Radon's Theorem (the r=2 case of Tverberg, included pedagogically as a warm-up) has no explicit counterpart in paper B. Paper B works directly with Tverberg in full generality and never separately states Radon.

Paper A defines convex hull explicitly as a Level-1 definition for its expository audience. Paper B uses convex hull pervasively (notation conv(.)) but does not extract a definition node for it; the closest definitional infrastructure in B (DP420.1 general position, DP420.2 crossing polytopes, DP420.4 Tverberg point) is at a higher level. No defensible counterpart exists.

Paper A's central tool is Barany's Colorful Caratheodory theorem (origin: external), used to drive the proof of Tverberg. Paper B never invokes Colorful Caratheodory; its own external Caratheodory citation (TP420.9) is the classical (non-colorful) version, which plays a different role (trimming oversized parts in PP420.1). The two are distinct theorems, so no match is emitted.

Paper A's proof of Tverberg (PP425.2) uses the lifting + Colorful Caratheodory route (Sarkaria-style). Paper B does not reprove Tverberg; it cites it. There is no proof-of-Tverberg node in B to align against. The crossing-strengthening proofs in B (PP420.3, PP420.4) are structurally different (unnesting + parity, not lifting + Colorful Caratheodory).
Paper A's proof of Radon's theorem has no analogue in paper B for the same reason TP425.1 does not.

All five equation nodes in A (system (1), the lifting reformulation, system (1') for r=3, the auxiliary vectors phi_{j,i}, and equation (2)) are internal scaffolding of the lifting-to-Colorful-Caratheodory proof. They have no counterpart in paper B, which uses entirely different combinatorial machinery (cocycles, coboundaries, parity).

Paper A's remark that the r=3 proof generalizes to arbitrary r is an expository hedge with no parallel in paper B. (Per §Compactness, remarks normally do not require none entries; this is included because A explicitly flags it as the bridge from r=3 to general r and the absence in B is a meaningful asymmetry.)
Paper A's remark that Radon is the r=2 case of Tverberg has no node in B. Listed for completeness; remarks are not strictly required to appear (per §Compactness).
